title: The Transistor: Bell Labs' Replacement for the Vacuum Tube (1947)
explainer: Every logic gate, register, and arithmetic unit in the architecture you're studying is built from transistors, and the transistor itself was demonstrated at Bell Labs in December 1947 by John Bardeen, Walter Brattain, and William Shockley as a small, reliable solid-state alternative to bulky, power-hungry, failure-prone vacuum tubes. Shrinking and multiplying that one device is what eventually made it physically possible to pack millions of gates onto a single chip; the three inventors shared the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physics for the work.
